s1.syndrome_frame: A cutaneous vascular lesion with telangiectasias on the lower extremity in a patient with a history of rectal adenocarcinoma and metastases
salient_findings: A single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque on the lower right lateral shin
Discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels with superficial, small lobules of small-caliber vessels on histopathological analysis
KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R somatic mutation identified on genetic analysis
key_facts: The patient is a man in his 40s
The patient has stage IV KRAS wild-type rectal adenocarcinoma
The patient has pulmonary and liver metastases
The patient has a history of radiation therapy and multiple chemotherapy cycles
The lesion is not associated with pain or pruritus
The lesion is a single, well-defined, blanchable bright red plaque
The lesion is densely composed of telangiectasias
The lesion grew to 4 cm in size
The epidermis is normal on histopathological analysis
The patient was enrolled in trial E7208 and received combination therapy every 2 weeks

shortlist.label: Acquired Tufted Angioma
shortlist.why_kept: Matches the clinical presentation of a single, well-defined, blanchable red plaque with telangiectasias and normal epidermis on histopathological analysis

shortlist.label: Pyogenic Granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Consistent with the appearance of a bright red plaque densely composed of telangiectasias, although the lack of pain or pruritus is less typical

shortlist.label: Microvenular Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Could be considered given the histopathological findings of small-caliber vessels, but the clinical context and growth pattern are less typical

shortlist.label: Glomeruloid Hemangioma
shortlist.why_kept: Possible diagnosis due to the presence of telangiectasias, but the clinical presentation and histopathological features are not as strongly supportive as for Acquired Tufted Angioma

shortlist.label: Bacillary Angiomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Although less likely, this diagnosis cannot be entirely excluded without further investigation, given the patient's history of immunosuppression due to cancer treatment

raw.rationale: The presence of discrete clusters of small-caliber vessels and superficial, small lobules of small-caliber vessels on histopathological analysis, along with the identification of a KDR (VEGFR2) c.C2312G, p.T771R somatic mutation, supports the diagnosis of Acquired Tufted Angioma.

rejected.label: Pyogenic Granuloma
rejected.why: While pyogenic granuloma can present as a bright red plaque, the histopathological findings and genetic analysis do not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Microvenular Hemangioma
rejected.why: The histopathological features do not match those typically seen in microvenular hemangioma, which is characterized by a reticular pattern of small vessels.

rejected.label: Glomeruloid Hemangioma
rejected.why: The clinical and histological features do not support a diagnosis of glomeruloid hemangioma, which is typically associated with POEMS syndrome.

rejected.label: Bacillary Angiomatosis
rejected.why: The absence of systemic symptoms and the lack of evidence of Bartonella infection make bacillary angiomatosis an unlikely diagnosis.
